The agent finds the cause of injected faults by reading Linux kernel traces. The context window was almost empty: across 720 runs, the single largest prompt used only 5.75% of it. Yet a third of all tool results (3,827 of 11,189) were cut before they reached the model, and every cut result became broken JSON. The harness cut each result by slicing its JSON text at a fixed length. This does not shorten a result evenly. It deletes whatever data sits near the end. One field reached the model in only 4.7% of calls. A second field, in the very same results, reached the model in 99.3% of calls. Which field held the fault's evidence depended on when the faulty process started: early or late in the trace. The agent's diagnosis accuracy matched this same split. So we ran controlled experiments to test one question: did the data loss cause the drop in accuracy? This paper makes four contributions. First, we model an agent's context as a five-stage pipeline, with a measured failure at each stage. Second, we replay 864 real tool results, including one from a production trace where the shipped cut deletes all 128 records of the fault's evidence. Third, a controlled experiment shows that the cut's real cost appears first as extra work, not as wrong answers: 43% more tool calls, twice the computation, and yield falling from 0.61 to 0.31. The agent still finds the right answer when it has another way to reach it. Fourth, a survey of seven agent frameworks finds two that cut tool output the same unsafe way. Whether the data cut truly causes the accuracy drop is still an open question.

papers.title: Stratum: Repository Memory for Coding Agents Beyond the Context Window
papers.summary: Context windows have grown a thousand-fold, yet coding agents still start every session with no memory of their past work. They re-read files, retry failed approaches, and forget root causes they established hours earlier. This is not a context-length problem but a memory-architecture problem. Our hypothesis: coding agents need persistent, experience-aware repository memory, so that knowledge survives from one session to the next. Three measurements on real repositories motivate the design. First, mid-size projects already exceed the largest production context windows, and storing knowledge inside the model's key-value (KV) cache costs $10^4$ to $10^5$ times more bytes than storing it as indexed text. Second, across 752 real bug-fix commits, the median fix edits two files, and these files plus their direct imports amount to less than 10% of the repository; the bottleneck is selection, not capacity. Third, even with transitive import reachability and test links, 47% of co-edited file pairs remain structurally disconnected; the knowledge needed for selection must be mined from history and experience. We sketch Stratum, a tiered memory that lives with the repository and serves it through page-safe tools: every response states what was returned, what remains, and what it cost. Retrieval over a store of one million nodes takes 1.7 ms at the median. In a multi-session experiment on eight real bugs, a fresh agent that inherited a prior session's memory, written by a different model, identified the root-cause file in 21 of 24 trials versus 6 of 24 for a retrieval-only baseline (Fisher $p<10^{-4}$), at 4.5x lower median token cost. With the notes of all eight investigations pooled in one store, success remained 8/8.

papers.title: Can AI Guide Testing Without Generating Tests? A Comparative Study of AI-Assisted Unit Testing
papers.summary: Recent advances in generative AI have enabled assistants to generate increasingly sophisticated executable unit tests. However, novices may accept these outputs without independently identifying what to test, evaluating test-suite completeness, or verifying correctness, potentially limiting opportunities to develop essential testing skills. Although prior work has explored AI-assisted test generation and feedback-oriented programming tutors, little is known about whether AI can support novices' testing practices without generating tests for them. To investigate this, we introduce TestCompass, a generative AI tutor that provides targeted feedback on weaknesses in students' test suites without generating executable tests. In a classroom study with 18 students, we compared TestCompass with a general AI assistant across two Java unit-testing tasks, examining students' testing behaviors, test-suite quality, and subjective experiences. We found that participants using the general-purpose AI assistant produced more tests, whereas TestCompass participants spent more time developing and verifying tests themselves. However, most test-suite quality measures were comparable between conditions, and TestCompass participants achieved similar requirement coverage with significantly fewer test methods ($p=0.012$) in one task. Neither group reported short-term improvements in perceived testing knowledge or confidence. These findings suggest that feedback-oriented AI can support meaningful testing outcomes while preserving opportunities for hands-on testing practice, offering a complementary approach to AI-assisted testing education.

papers.title: Agent or Human? Detecting Commits by AI Coding Agents in the Absence of Authorship Signatures
papers.summary: AI coding agents such as Claude Code, GitHub Copilot coding agent, and Cursor now commit directly to open-source repositories. Empirical studies of these agents identify their commits through authorship signatures, such as bot accounts and Co-authored-by trailers. These signatures are optional, can be removed, and are often attached to pull requests rather than to individual commits. Hence, it is unclear whether Agent commits can be told apart from Human commits once the signatures are gone. We investigate the signals and limits of signature-free detection using 7,837,946 commits from 1,226 repositories, covering five coding agents and Human commits. After signatures are masked, detectors rank Agent commits above Human commits with a ROC AUC of up to 0.859, and most of this signal comes from message verbosity and change size rather than from the code itself. On the shared sample, gpt-6-sol without fine-tuning reaches AUCs similar to XGBoost and TF-IDF. At the observed Agent share, however, the best detector on the full test set reaches a precision of only 0.332. Detection transfers poorly to held-out Claude Code and Copilot, with TF-IDF reaching an AUC of only 0.524 for Claude Code. Temporal changes also depend on the agent, e.g., Copilot AUC drops and later recovers, while more training history helps Claude Code but not Copilot. These results indicate that signature-free detection can prioritize commits for review but cannot replace recorded attribution, and that studies relying on signature-based labels should treat them as a lower bound on agent activity.

papers.title: Instant Software Factories
papers.summary: Coding agents can quickly build prototypes, but a long tail of fixes, optimizations, tests, and releases separates a prototype from a product. A software factory handles this ongoing work through a repeatable process. We ask whether this work needs dedicated orchestration and how such factories should be judged. Given a tested repository and a coding agent, an instant software factory uses only two coordination inputs, a swarm of cron-job agents with standing objectives and a shared communication board, such as GitHub, where agents coordinate through the traces they leave. We developed a bootstrap prompt designed to set up both inputs from one round of human input, with governance as a separable layer. We distilled it from two manually configured industrial factories, observed for 15 and 17 days, and have not yet evaluated it. In the GitHub-coordinated CLI factory, daily merges rose 15x during agent rollout, an observed association. Its agents also filed 95% of new issues and authored 40 of 58 PRs that changed CI workflows, and at least 5.6% of issues marked as fixed were later found to have incorrect fixes. Unlike an agent scored on a fixed benchmark, a factory thus changes its own workload, evaluator, and measured progress. We formulate factory development as multi-objective optimization under this endogenous feedback. Over five months, we plan to evolve both factories, test the bootstrap on new repositories, and test five falsifiable hypotheses.

papers.title: Your Wish Is My Commit: Over-Compliant Refactoring in AI Coding Agents
papers.summary: Large language models are known to be sycophantic, over-complying with users even when doing so is unproductive. When these models act as coding agents, this can be costly: an agent that keeps editing after no edit improves the code writes churn, technical debt, and review burden into the codebase. Yet the consequences of sycophancy in software engineering remain largely understudied. To understand them, we run a controlled study of iterative refactoring, an open-ended task with no stopping criterion, where any edit an agent makes once the code is already clean reflects compliance rather than improvement. Across algorithmic (n=50) and object-oriented (n=10) suites, we repeatedly ask two widely used agents, Codex and Claude Code, to refactor further across five models. Over 3,000 turns, we define six behavioral signals of over-compliance. We hypothesized that a capable agent would stop once it recognized an optimized codebase; none did. Every model kept editing, rewriting up to 31x the original codebase before first stopping and resuming edits even after declaring the task complete. Over-compliance is a costly, multi-turn behavior that compounds with every turn, and our six signals give developers and tool builders a way to detect and curb it.
papers.title_zh: 你的愿望就是我的提交：AI 编程智能体中的过度顺从式重构
papers.abstract_zh: 大型语言模型已知会表现出谄媚倾向，即使这样做毫无成效，也会过度顺应用户。当这些模型充当编程智能体时，这会带来高昂代价：一个智能体如果在没有任何编辑能改进代码之后仍继续编辑，就会把代码搅动、技术债务和审查负担写入代码库。然而，软件工程中谄媚倾向的后果在很大程度上仍缺乏研究。为了理解这些后果，我们对迭代式重构进行了一项受控研究；迭代式重构是一项没有停止标准的开放式任务，其中一旦代码已经整洁，智能体所做的任何编辑反映的都是顺从，而非改进。在算法（n=50）和面向对象（n=10）套件中，我们针对五个模型，反复要求两个广泛使用的智能体——Codex 和 Claude Code——进一步重构。在超过 3,000 轮中，我们定义了过度顺从的六种行为信号。我们假设，一个有能力的智能体一旦识别出已优化的代码库就会停止；但没有任何一个这样做。每个模型都持续编辑，在首次停止之前重写了高达原始代码库 31 倍的代码，并且即使在声明任务完成后仍会恢复编辑。过度顺从是一种代价高昂的多轮行为，且会随着每一轮而累积；我们的六种信号为开发者和工具构建者提供了一种检测并遏制它的方法。

papers.title: When AI Can Build It, What Should We Assess? Rethinking Evidence of Engineering Competence
papers.summary: Generative AI can produce code, tests, documentation, and technical explanations that resemble artefacts traditionally used as evidence of student competence, weakening the inference from artefact quality to the engineering capability behind it. We report the redesign and first deployment of a 13-week, AI-permissive, software-intensive engineering course in which students may delegate substantial work to AI while retaining responsibility for planning, verification, review, integration, and explanation. The redesign couples an engineering accountability workflow, which structures human-AI work and preserves human decision authority, with an assessment evidence architecture comprising six complementary channels: product, process/origin, verification, explanation, reflection, and individual assurance. A collect--cross-check--escalate (CCE) reasoning logic connects these channels rather than treating any single artefact or trace as sufficient evidence of competence. By the end of Week 11, the deployment involved 87 students organised into 17 teams, with 957 individual weekly Git repositories and 34 group-project Git repositories supporting repeated assessment and engineering activity. The first deployment yielded four practical lessons: AI assistance changes where rubric criteria carry evidential weight; multiple evidence channels require deliberate cross-checking and meaningful complementarity; the evidential strength realised in practice may differ from that intended in the assessment design; and automation scales evidence collection more readily than interpretation. The contribution is a conceptually grounded, deployed design for making engineering responsibility and competence more visible when AI can perform substantial artefact production.

papers.title: ProCerDCL: Query-Efficient Black-Box Probabilistic Verification of Deep Learning Compiler Optimization
papers.summary: We present \tool, a query-efficient framework for black-box probabilistic verification. Given a fixed, sampleable input distribution and a binary property oracle, \tool assesses the property's violation probability $p$ against a threshold $θ$. Under independent sampling and stateless oracle behavior, acceptance asserts $p\leθ$, rejection asserts $p>θ+η$ for a user-specified separation margin, and an inconclusive verdict indicates insufficient evidence for either conclusion. The probability of each type of erroneous verdict is bounded by its specified error budget. To support this three-valued contract efficiently, \tool uses a single sequential test, eliminating the interval family required by the baseline. The test accounts for repeated sampling checks through either corrected exact binomial confidence intervals or an anytime-valid confidence sequence. We apply \tool to probabilistic local model semantic consistency, where the property oracle detects decision-level inconsistencies between reference and compiled executions under a specified perturbation distribution. Our evaluation covers 24 tasks across TorchInductor and TensorRT and examines sampling efficiency, conclusiveness, and diagnostic behavior. For sampling efficiency, we use paired one-model clean-label radius searches: the baseline requires 3.6-4.2 times as many unique samples under matched numerical parameters while providing a weaker decision contract. For model semantic consistency, checks at $θ=10^{-3}$ yield 817 acceptances, 19 inconclusive verdicts, and 4 rejections across 840 input--backend instances from 21 tasks. Case studies of two documented compiler faults further demonstrate what these local verdicts can diagnose.

papers.title: From Ripple to Boundary: Deterministic Impact Boundaries for LLM-Based Software Evolution
papers.summary: The landscape of software evolution is undergoing a fundamental paradigm shift in the era of Large Language Models. As industrial software engineering increasingly transitions toward design-driven code generation, the bottleneck of evolution has shifted from writing code to maintaining deterministic consistency between multi-source design assets and the generated code. When a design asset changes, LLM agents currently lack a deterministic impact boundary to identify which code must be evolved, leading to two failure modes: hallucinating missing changes or breaking unrelated code. Probabilistic approaches, such as semantic retrieval or text-based diffing, fail to capture the structural ripple effects across highly interconnected design dependencies. We propose a paradigm shift from probabilistic semantic retrieval to deterministic structural constraints. We formalize the design assets as a Knowledge Graph and organize them into a content-addressed Merkle Directed Acyclic Graph. Our key insight reveals a topological isomorphism between the logical ripple effect of a design change and the content hash propagation within the DAG. By leveraging this, we transform ambiguous impact analysis into verifiable structural operations. Through a two-phase diffing process, we extract a precise causal chain that defines the exact modification boundary. This boundary enables deterministic context injection, providing the LLM agent with strictly scoped code and design updates, thereby fundamentally guaranteeing evolution safety. As a by-product, the KG serves as an agent-queryable knowledge base for natural language design retrieval. Early deployment on a large-scale industrial payment platform demonstrates that our mechanism successfully computes the exact impact boundary and generates incremental code modifications that meet the expected design changes.
papers.title_zh: 从涟漪到边界：面向基于大语言模型的软件演化的确定性影响边界
papers.abstract_zh: 在大语言模型时代，软件演化的格局正在经历根本性的范式转变。随着工业软件工程日益转向设计驱动的代码生成，演化的瓶颈已从编写代码转移至维护多源设计资产与所生成代码之间的确定性一致性。当某个设计资产发生变化时，LLM 智能体目前缺乏一个确定性的影响边界来识别哪些代码必须被演化，这导致两种失败模式：臆造出缺失的变更，或破坏无关的代码。概率性方法，例如语义检索或基于文本的差异比较，无法捕捉跨越高度互联的设计依赖关系所产生的结构性涟漪效应。我们提出一种从概率性语义检索转向确定性结构约束的范式转变。我们将设计资产形式化为一个知识图谱，并将其组织为一个内容寻址的 Merkle 有向无环图。我们的关键洞见揭示了设计变更的逻辑涟漪效应与 DAG 内内容哈希传播之间的拓扑同构关系。借助这一点，我们将模糊的影响分析转化为可验证的结构性操作。通过一个两阶段的差异比较过程，我们提取出一条精确的因果链，用以定义确切的修改边界。该边界使确定性的上下文注入成为可能，为 LLM 智能体提供严格限定范围的代码与设计更新，从而从根本上保证演化安全性。作为一个副产品，该知识图谱可作为可供智能体查询的知识库，用于自然语言设计检索。在一个大规模工业支付平台上的早期部署表明，我们的机制成功计算出了确切的影响边界，并生成了符合预期设计变更的增量代码修改。

papers.title: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Behaviorally Adequate Test Generation from Software Requirements
papers.summary: As large language model agents increasingly compile natural-language requirements into repository-level code, requirement-to-test generation grows in importance to provide validation constraints (or harness) to guide code generation. Yet it remains unclear whether current agents can generate tests that validate the required behavior when the implementation of that behavior is withheld. Existing test-generation benchmarks mostly focus on white-box testing, whereas the requirement--test-related study usually requires evaluation on semantic alignment between the given documents and the generated tests. We introduce Req2Test-Bench, a benchmark containing 5,086 execution-validated instances recovered from developer-authored behavior-driven development (BDD) artifacts in 8 open-source projects, spanning 5 programming languages and 4 BDD frameworks. Each instance pairs a natural-language requirement in Gherkin with its developer-written Test Implementation. Given the requirement, target interfaces of the required behavior, an agent must generate a complete, potentially multi-file Test Implementation. Evaluation of 8 agent--model--reasoning configurations reveals a substantial gap between execution success and behavioral adequacy, which is measured strictly as kill-completeness: a kill-complete test kills every mutant that the ground-truth test kills. The best-performing configuration, Codex with DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, produces passing tests for 82.8% of instances, yet only 33.8% are behaviorally adequate. We find that (1) scaling up agents yields sharply diminishing returns in behavioral adequacy relative to generation cost; (2) under-specified requirements cause the information gap, including ambiguous setup and implicit expected outcomes; and (3) requirement-grounded harnesses that steer agent non-determinism offer a promising direction for improvement.
papers.title_zh: 对从软件需求生成行为充分测试的LLM智能体进行基准测试
papers.abstract_zh: 随着大型语言模型智能体越来越多地将自然语言需求编译为仓库级代码，从需求到测试的生成在提供验证约束（或测试装置）以指导代码生成方面变得日益重要。然而，目前尚不清楚当前智能体在所需行为的实现被隐藏时，是否能够生成验证所需行为的测试。现有的测试生成基准主要关注白盒测试，而需求—测试相关研究通常要求评估给定文档与生成测试之间的语义对齐。我们提出了Req2Test-Bench，这是一个包含5,086个经过执行验证的实例的基准，这些实例从8个开源项目中由开发者编写的行为驱动开发（BDD）工件中恢复而来，涵盖5种编程语言和4种BDD框架。每个实例将一个用Gherkin编写的自然语言需求与其由开发者编写的测试实现配对。给定该需求以及所需行为的目标接口，智能体必须生成一个完整的、可能跨多个文件的测试实现。对8种智能体—模型—推理配置的评估揭示了执行成功与行为充分性之间的显著差距；行为充分性被严格地以杀死完备性（kill-completeness）来衡量：一个杀死完备的测试会杀死真实测试所杀死的每一个变异体。表现最佳的配置是Codex搭配DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash，它为82.8%的实例生成了通过测试，但只有33.8%的实例在行为上是充分的。我们发现：(1) 扩大智能体规模相对于生成成本而言，在行为充分性上带来急剧递减的回报；(2) 未充分指定的需求造成了信息差距，包括模糊的设置和隐含的预期结果；(3) 以需求为基础的测试装置能够引导智能体的非确定性，为改进提供了一个有前景的方向。

papers.title: A Fine-Grained Empirical Study of Upstream Security Events and Downstream Mitigation in Maven
papers.summary: Open-source vulnerability mitigation spans upstream libraries and the downstream projects that depend on them. Upstream, a vulnerability progresses through a public report when one exists, a fix, a fixed release, and NVD disclosure. Downstream, a project mitigates it by adopting the fixed release, and the timeliness of this adoption is measured relative to these events. Prior work studies the two sides separately, so it is unclear whether downstream exposure stems from delayed upstream release, delayed downstream adoption, or both. We address this gap by following 832 CVEs in the Maven ecosystem from the upstream fix to its adoption by each exposed downstream project. We classify upstream fixes as \textit{silent} or \textit{transparent}, recover the order of report, fix, release, and NVD disclosure, and link vulnerable artifacts to their downstream dependents. We then compare this order with downstream adoption and dependabot usage. We find that delay arises on both sides. Upstream, the fixed release comes before NVD disclosure for about 82\% of CVEs, for both silent and transparent fixes. For the other 17.9\%, downstream projects have no fix to adopt for days to more than four months after disclosure. Downstream, exposure is concentrated, with the top 10\% of CVEs accounting for 72.1\% of it. Of 1,677 observed adoptions, 85.3\% happen after NVD disclosure, rising to 88.3\% for silent fixes released before disclosure. Most adoptions come through routine dependency updates. Adoptions with dependabot version updates have a median release-to-adoption delay of 10.4 days, compared with 110.6 days without dependabot. Yet version updates were configured at adoption time for only 8.5\% of total adoptions. We translate these findings into implications for upstream maintainers, downstream developers, and dependency-automation tools.

papers.title: ASNER: Software Architecture Recovery with Adaptive Semantic Neighborhoods and Evidence-Grounded Refinement
papers.summary: Automated software architecture recovery provides architectural context for software engineering and repository-level LLM agents. Existing methods combine structural and semantic signals, but functional relatedness does not necessarily imply shared architectural responsibility. Fixed thresholds or Top-K neighborhoods also ignore repository scale and local similarity distributions, introducing errors that propagate through clustering. Unconstrained LLM refinement may further alter correct assignments without sufficient evidence. We propose ASNER (Adaptive Semantic Neighborhoods and Evidence-Grounded Refinement for Software Architecture Recovery), based on responsibility-aware, project-adaptive relation modeling and evidence-grounded boundary verification. ASNER derives structured file responsibilities with an LLM, constructs semantic neighborhoods that adapt to repository scale and local similarity distributions, and augments a static dependency graph with selected semantic relations and weak directory cues. Community detection recovers the component backbone. A Responsibility-Ownership-Aware (ROA) Agent then examines uncertain boundary files using project-level responsibilities and traceable code evidence, changing assignments only when supported. Experiments on 12 open-source projects spanning C, C++, Java, and Python show that ASNER achieves the best macro-average on all five metrics on the common benchmark, improving ARI and c2c@66 over GAER-GAT by 19.5% and 32.9%, respectively. A downstream evaluation shows that ASNER-guided LocAgent improves file-, module-, and function-level code localization, demonstrating the value of its architectural context for repository-level software engineering tasks.

papers.title: A lightweight C Code Generator for Heterogeneous TinyML Systems
papers.summary: Over the past decade, the significant advancements in artificial intelligence have been closely tied to increasingly sophisticated training frameworks and steadily powerful computing hardware. However, the entire ecosystem remains fragmented. On one hand, models are represented with frameworks dependent formats, while on the other hand, new tailored hardware for accelerating novel operators has continued to emerge. To effectively diminish the transfer costs from training to inference, we propose a lightweight C code generator designed for bare-metal heterogeneous systems that incorporate domain-specific accelerators. Through a comprehensive case study on a RISC-V based radar DSP, we demonstrate that by employing an accelerator with ahead-of-time optimizations like weight tuning and bias fusion, our approach achieves a 2.3 times improvement in inference speed and a 20% reduction in binary size compared to the microTVM flow registered with the same accelerator, thus offering another compelling choice for resource-constrained edge devices. The code is open-sourced in Gitlab.

papers.title: Beyond QASecClaw: Agent Scaling, Verifier Feedback, and Evidence Reliability in Software Assurance
papers.summary: Can additional specialist language-model contexts improve software assurance when deterministic tool evidence is already available? We study this question through five experiments spanning authored Java warning controls, OWASP Benchmark assessment, Defects4J test generation, SV-COMP assertion verdicts, and deliberately misleading evidence packages. The evaluated systems use Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct, with a 1.5B sensitivity analysis, and complete 13,638 model requests. On eight related development warnings, increasing the context count from 1 to 50 increases token use 49-fold without improving unsafe clearance. On 160 OWASP cases, model configurations trade clearance against unresolved outcomes; the ten-context arm assesses only 96 cases. On 32 SV-COMP tasks, raw verifier feedback raises mean correct model verdicts from 12.7 to 22.0, but also raises incorrect verdicts from one to seven; a JBMC-plus-JVM validation baseline returns 26 correct verdicts and six unresolved outcomes. On two sets of 120 evidence packages, models reject 70-100% of applicable counterexamples, while construction-specific scope checks classify every package correctly. No target defect is discovered in three Defects4J bugs, one unsupported by the test adapter. These descriptive results support deterministic evidence admission for the tested settings, while exposing limits of verdict aggregation, feedback interpretation, and the available evaluation coverage.

papers.title: Does More Thinking Pay Off? Reasoning Cost and Correctness of LLMs in Code Generation and Bug Fixing
papers.summary: Many LLMs now emit an explicit reasoning trace before they write code, but benchmark results for code generation and bug fixing usually report correctness alone. It is therefore unclear how much the extra reasoning contributes relative to the tokens it consumes. We examine this question with 866 Python tasks drawn from HumanEval Pro, MBPP Pro, and BugsInPy under five model settings. We look at the accuracy gain and token overhead of reasoning, the behaviors that appear inside reasoning traces, and whether a shortened trace still leads to a correct solution. Turning reasoning on in Qwen3-32B over five runs improves mean pass@1 on HumanEval Pro from 71.1% to 76.5% and mean tests pass on BugsInPy from 3.5% to 7.9%. On MBPP Pro the improvement from 68.1% to 69.5% is not statistically significant, even though the model uses a median of over 2,000 thinking tokens per task. Across models, a longer median trace does not reliably mean higher accuracy. A qualitative analysis shows that traces mostly choose and check an implementation in code generation, while in bug fixing they mostly locate the fault and plan the repair. We then truncate stored traces offline and ask Qwen3-32B with reasoning off to produce a solution from what remains. Retaining the first half of a trace yields no statistically significant drop in correctness. Stopping when the trace becomes repetitive seldom triggers, and stopping once solution code first appears benefits some models but harms others. Neither rule beats plain fixed truncation. These results suggest that more reasoning is not always better and that studies should report reasoning cost alongside correctness.

papers.title: Toward Circuit-Aware Mutation Testing for Quantum Programs: Exact Visibility and Execution Planning
papers.summary: Mutation testing assesses test suites by introducing program changes and checking whether tests detect them. In quantum programs, a surviving mutant may leave program behavior unchanged, produce a change hidden by the chosen input or measurement, or remain undetected because statistical evidence is insufficient. We develop a circuit-aware framework to distinguish these causes and guide execution planning and test changes. The framework covers ideal, noiseless programs and mutations that replace one gate or subcircuit. The method traces how a mutation can affect measured outputs and combines established mathematical checks with statistical estimates. For supported cases, we establish conditions under which a test cannot reveal a mutation and exact formulas for its effect when the required state information is available. Under stated assumptions, we bound the mutation score while retaining surviving and unresolved mutants, and identify a restricted circuit family whose mutation effects admit efficient classical classification. The deliverables include a decision procedure, mathematical guarantees, worked examples of test changes and their implementation requirements, and a small-circuit reference implementation for differential expectation tests. These results help testers decide what to execute, what to change, and what remains unknown. The evidence is limited to proofs and executable examples under the ideal model.

papers.title: Spine: Compiling Subtask Trees into Structured Context for Long-Horizon Coding Agents
papers.summary: Long-horizon coding tasks contain nested subtasks. Typically, agents record interactions sequentially into a growing history, causing context inflation and performance degradation. Compressing or trimming the history without explicit subtask boundaries can discard information needed by unfinished subtasks. Conversely, recursive subagent delegation isolates completed subtasks through child agents by assigning every subtask boundary to delegation, which conflates subtask granularity with executing agent choice, adding execution and coordination overhead. We introduce Spine, an interface and runtime that align model context with subtask nesting and completion. An agent declares explicit subtask boundaries through work scopes, allowing the same agent to execute nested subtasks inline while reserving delegation for independent parallel tasks. The runtime organizes execution in SpineTree, a persistent tree recording subtask relations, local interactions, completion states, and returned results. Before each model call, it compiles the tree into model context just in time, retaining unfinished subtasks' interactions and replacing completed subtasks' details with their results, while preserving prefix-cache reuse. We integrate Spine into Codex to build SpineCodex. With GPT-5.6 Sol, compared with native Codex, SpineCodex improves SWE-Milestone Score by 11.8% while reducing total cost by 32.4%, improves the average ProgramBench test-pass rate by 17.3%, and improves Mean@5 on eight of the ten evaluated FrontierSWE tasks. On SWE-Milestone, it also achieves a comparable Score to Recursive Subagent at 73.7% lower total cost. We also integrate Spine into Pi through a reusable software package: with Gemini 3.8 Flash and Qwen 3.8 27B, it improves SWE-Milestone Score by 9.5-17.5% and the average ProgramBench test-pass rate by 4.3-8.7% compared with native Pi.

papers.title: BenchMeUp: Building Software Engineering Benchmarks from Natural-Language Specifications
papers.summary: Software-engineering research relies on benchmarks that evaluate new techniques on a set of problem instances. Unfortunately, manually constructing benchmarks is labor-intensive, as researchers must find suitable instances, prepare execution environments, establish expected outcomes, and validate correctness. This paper presents BenchMeUp, an approach for automatically creating software-engineering benchmarks from natural-language specifications. Given a specification defining the desired instances, data sources, and evaluation procedures, BenchMeUp generates search rules and a construction plan, invokes parallel LLM agents that identify candidate instances and construct executable instances, validates the results in fresh execution environments, and packages the instances behind a unified command-line interface. We evaluate the approach on four tasks: program repair, issue reproduction, compiler autotuning, and fixing static-analysis warnings. Targeting 50 instances per task (200 in total), BenchMeUp constructs 198 instances, of which 196 (99\%) are successfully packaged. Search and construction take 36 minutes and \$0.79 per instance, on average. Evaluating eight existing techniques on the generated benchmarks, we find that 189 of 196 packaged instances (96\%) support end-to-end evaluation, allowing users to study the effectiveness of the techniques. Checking every constructed instance against its source, the specification, and its expected outcome, we find that 180 of 198 (91\%) meet all criteria, compared with 10 of 200 instances delivered by Codex (general-purpose coding agent). Overall, we show that LLM-based agents can automate benchmark construction across diverse software-engineering tasks and produce executable instances that existing techniques can use, while validity beyond execution still needs to be checked.

papers.title: Hidden in Plain Sight: an Empirical Study about The Instruction Stacks of Coding Agents
papers.summary: Coding agents send their models more than the user's prompt: they add instructions, tool definitions, and environmental context that form an instruction stack. This stack guides execution and changes across releases, yet remains largely unexposed to users and insufficiently characterized in research. We present a longitudinal, cross-agent study of the instruction stacks captured in the first model requests of 1,886 releases of Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Qwen Code, and OpenCode. Under controlled conditions, we analyze their composition and evolution and trace changes in the four open-source agents to documented motivations. Our findings show why examining the system prompt or reporting the model alone provides an incomplete account of agent inputs. Tool definitions dominate three agents' latest requests, while occasional concentrated revisions alter instructions governing tool use, attribution, and coding style. Such revisions can complicate how researchers identify agent-authored contributions and interpret generated code. We also found that only 48% of examined change units directly explain the motivation for stack revisions. Across agents, shared capabilities emerge despite increasingly distinct wording. These findings expose an evolving, incompletely documented layer of agent design. The findings motivate documenting captured instruction stacks alongside agent releases, models, and user prompts, and preserving the rationale behind their revisions.

papers.title: Mind the Intent Gap: A Methodology for Collaborative Agent-Driven Software Engineering
papers.summary: AI agents have entered software teams, first as tools and now as team members. They produce in minutes what used to take days, yet the expected gain in delivery often fails to appear. We argue that they are entering processes designed for people, which quietly relied on people to cover three of their weaknesses. The team's intent was never fully written down, because colleagues filled the gaps. An AI agent fills them too, though by guessing, and drifts from what the team had in mind. The reasoning behind each deliverable was already lost from one step to the next, and AI agents now inflate and deflate the documents passed along. The reasoning people did alone was partly private and now moves into AI tools that keep it private by nature. We present CAIA, for Collaborative Agentic Intent Alignment, a methodology for software teams that brings agents into the way they work. A knowledge base describes the product that a project maintains. For each Change, a micro-team aligns on its intent before agents evolve the product and propose updates to the Knowledge Base. The proposed CAIA methodology emerged from an industrial need and is already in use at Ni2, with a platform built to support it. We present the methodology and outline our plans to evaluate it further.

papers.title: HIDE: Hierarchical Isolation via Documentation and Evidence for Rustc Bugs
papers.summary: Rustc bugs can prevent valid programs from compiling or cause incorrect compilation results, making the identification of responsible source files essential for repair. Using large language models (LLMs) for rustc bug isolation raises three challenges. First, distributed compiler functionality requires understanding both what individual files do and how they work together. Second, a large source file search space makes exhaustive analysis of all files costly. Third, including documentation and source code for many candidate files in LLM prompts leads to context overload, which can reduce bug isolation accuracy. We propose HIDE, a hierarchical LLM-based approach that combines compiler documentation with bug evidence to rank suspicious rustc source files. Given a rustc revision and a bug context, HIDE consists of two stages that generate compiler documentation and narrow the search space. To understand distributed compiler functionality, the Layered Documentation Aggregation stage summarizes what individual files do and how files with similar functions work together. To reduce the large source file search space, the Hierarchical Bug Isolation stage uses hierarchical candidate selection to reduce the number of files requiring detailed analysis. To mitigate context overload, this stage uses Scoped Candidate Competition and Evidence-Guided Code Slicing to limit the number of candidates and the amount of source code included in each prompt, respectively. We evaluate HIDE on 160 reproducible rustc bugs and compare it with Agentless, SoapFL, and GraphLocator. With GPT-5.4, HIDE achieves 42.08% Accuracy@1 and 80.42% Accuracy@10, exceeding the strongest baseline results by 5.83% and 6.04%, respectively. These results demonstrate that generating compiler documentation, narrowing candidates hierarchically, and limiting analysis context enable effective rustc bug isolation.
papers.title_zh: HIDE：面向 Rustc 缺陷的基于文档与证据的分层隔离
papers.abstract_zh: Rustc 缺陷可能导致有效程序无法编译，或导致不正确的编译结果，因此识别应负责的源文件对于修复至关重要。使用大语言模型（LLMs）进行 rustc 缺陷隔离会带来三个挑战。第一，分布式的编译器功能要求理解各个文件的功能以及它们如何协同工作。第二，庞大的源文件搜索空间使得对所有文件进行穷尽分析代价高昂。第三，在 LLM 提示中包含许多候选文件的文档和源代码会导致上下文过载，从而可能降低缺陷隔离的准确性。我们提出 HIDE，一种基于 LLM 的分层方法，它将编译器文档与缺陷证据相结合，对可疑的 rustc 源文件进行排序。给定一个 rustc 修订版本和一个缺陷上下文，HIDE 由两个阶段组成，分别生成编译器文档并缩小搜索空间。为了理解分布式的编译器功能，分层文档聚合（Layered Documentation Aggregation）阶段总结各个文件的功能以及具有相似功能的文件如何协同工作。为了缩小庞大的源文件搜索空间，分层缺陷隔离（Hierarchical Bug Isolation）阶段使用分层候选选择来减少需要详细分析的文件数量。为了缓解上下文过载，该阶段分别使用限定范围的候选竞争（Scoped Candidate Competition）和证据引导的代码切片（Evidence-Guided Code Slicing）来限制候选数量以及每个提示中包含的源代码量。我们在 160 个可复现的 rustc 缺陷上评估 HIDE，并将其与 Agentless、SoapFL 和 GraphLocator 进行比较。在 GPT-5.4 下，HIDE 实现了 42.08% 的 Accuracy@1 和 80.42% 的 Accuracy@10，分别超过最强基线结果 5.83% 和 6.04%。这些结果表明，生成编译器文档、分层缩小候选范围以及限制分析上下文能够实现有效的 rustc 缺陷隔离。

papers.title: FeatureArc: Benchmarking Coding Agents on Evolving Features
papers.summary: A software feature usually evolves over time: developers extend its first version as new use cases and requirements arrive, and each extension builds on code written earlier. Most feature benchmarks evaluate a single request on a fixed codebase. Feature evolution requires evaluating successive extensions on an agent's own earlier code and checking whether the feature remains correct. We introduce FeatureArc to evaluate coding agents on evolving features, together with a pipeline that constructs its tasks from repository histories. The benchmark combines dependencies between successive stages of the same feature, explicit requirements and interface contracts, and executable checks across four programming languages. The pipeline validates fail-to-pass (F2P) tests for new behavior and pass-to-pass (P2P) tests for existing behavior on the reference code before and after each stage. We evaluated 10 coding agents on 73 manually reviewed tasks of 2 to 10 stages. Each agent works in one persistent session and workspace without external test feedback or rollback. The evaluation reveals a gap between first-stage and whole-feature success: pooled success falls from 62.7% at the first stage to 28.5% when the whole feature is tested on the final code. Trajectory analysis identifies inherited defects as a common failure mechanism, present in 72.9% of failed later stages. These earlier errors often remain undetected: in stages following a failure, agents leave the earlier error unnoticed about 95% of the time, and their self-tests rarely revisit earlier stages. Evolving a feature autonomously, without human checks between stages, therefore remains a substantial challenge for current coding agents. At Tencent, the pipeline extends internal evaluations to this setting and guides the development of Hunyuan, Tencent's family of large language models.
papers.title_zh: FeatureArc：在演化功能上对编码智能体进行基准测试
papers.abstract_zh: 软件功能通常会随时间演化：随着新用例和需求的到来，开发者会扩展其初始版本，而每一次扩展都建立在先前编写的代码之上。大多数功能基准测试在固定代码库上评估单个请求。功能演化则要求在智能体自己先前的代码上评估后续扩展，并检查该功能是否仍然正确。我们提出 FeatureArc，用于评估编码智能体在演化功能上的表现，并给出一个从仓库历史中构建其任务的流水线。该基准结合了同一功能连续阶段之间的依赖关系、显式需求和接口契约，以及跨四种编程语言的可执行检查。该流水线在每个阶段之前和之后，在参考代码上验证针对新行为的失败转通过（F2P）测试和针对现有行为的通过转通过（P2P）测试。我们在由2至10个阶段组成的73个人工审查任务上评估了10个编码智能体。每个智能体在一个持久会话和工作区中工作，不获得外部测试反馈，也不进行回滚。评估揭示了第一阶段成功与整个功能成功之间的差距：汇总成功率从第一阶段的62.7%下降到在最终代码上测试整个功能时的28.5%。轨迹分析将继承缺陷识别为一种常见失败机制，其出现在72.9%的后续失败阶段中。这些较早的错误往往未被发现：在失败之后的阶段中，智能体大约95%的情况下会让较早的错误保持未被注意，而且它们的自测很少重新审视较早阶段。因此，在没有阶段之间人工检查的情况下自主演化功能，对当前编码智能体而言仍然是一项重大挑战。在腾讯，该流水线将内部评估扩展到这一场景，并指导混元（Hunyuan）——腾讯的大语言模型系列——的开发。

papers.title: An EVM-Cosmos Bridge for Atomic, Semantic-Preserving Transfer of Environmental Tokens
papers.summary: Transferring semantically typed tokens between heterogeneous blockchains (e.g. EVM and Cosmos ecosystems) raises two problems: semantic mixing, the loss of a token's domainspecific meaning in transit (e.g., CO2 removals issued under different methodologies), and atomicity despite divergent consensus and timing assumptions. We propose a bridge that addresses both. A deterministic indicator identity derived from cryptographic commitments, mirrored in class registries on both chains and checked at mint time, preventing semantic mixing by construction. For atomicity, we extend hash time-locked contracts (HTLCs) from two-party exchange to single-owner transfer with an automatic callback that burns the source escrow after a destination claim, and a protocol-minimum bounty that makes the fallback burn incentive-compatible even against adversarial senders. We machine-check the protocol's invariants with TLC (supply conservation fails without the rational-monitor assumption and holds with it) and validate a bidirectional prototype on Polygon and Neutron mainnets over Axelar GMP: fully automatic transfers with a median end-to-end latency of 97 s over 50 Polygon to Neutron transfers across 7 days (all completed by the on-chain automatic callback) and 93 s in the reverse direction, and semantic-validation overhead below 0.4% of messaging cost. We also document the integration failure modes of Cosmos originated messaging, whose dominant operational risk proves to be relay eligibility rather than latency.

papers.title: Spectral Braids: A Topological Descriptor for Dynamic Directed Networks
papers.summary: Eigenvalues are a workhorse of graph machine learning: spectral clustering, spectral graph neural networks, and graph kernels all summarize a network by the eigenvalues of a matrix. These eigenvalues are almost always treated as a static list of numbers. When a graph changes, however, its eigenvalues move, and when the matrix is not symmetric, they move in the complex plane, where they can wind around each other. The pattern of this winding is a braid, a classical object from topology. We propose spectral braids, a methodology for dynamic directed networks: each snapshot is aggregated into a community-level transition matrix, its complex eigenvalues are tracked over time, and the braid they trace is read off as a word. The word is then mapped to a matrix by the Burau representation, which gives a fixed-size feature vector for any classifier. The braid has a concrete meaning: each eigenvalue describes how a group of communities behaves, and each crossing records one group overtaking another. We evaluate the method on dynamic network classification, using synthetic networks of online communities whose labels describe how the network evolved between the same starting and ending states. Our experimental results show that the proposed features reach 97.1% accuracy on four classes, against 44.5% for the best feature set that does not track eigenvalues, and that the Burau features also separate networks containing the same events in a different order, which simple counts of crossings cannot do. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study that defines braids and braid monodromy on graph data and uses them as features for learning on dynamic networks.

papers.title: Quantized Edge Inference of a Self-Supervised SAR-Optical Encoder on Commodity x86 Hardware
papers.summary: Self-supervised vision transformers are increasingly used as reusable encoders for Earth observation, but their inference cost on the hardware available in the field is rarely characterized. We deploy a pretrained SAR-optical masked-autoencoder encoder on three commodity x86 nodes, from a low-power CPU without AVX2 to an AVX2+VNNI reference, at FP32, FP16 and INT8 on the CPU and, where present, the integrated GPU, and report latency, energy (RAPL and wall plug) and linear-probe accuracy. Quantization is accuracy-neutral: INT8 changes micro-mAP by only +0.0006, within the seed spread, so precision becomes a pure cost decision. INT8 lowers CPU latency on every node, by 1.45x even on the CPU without AVX2, and CPU energy wherever it is measured, and the VNNI reference (1.53x) suggests a further gain beyond AVX2. The Pareto-optimal device shifts from the integrated GPU, which is 4.38x faster than the CPU on the weakest node, to the CPU as the CPU class improves.

papers.title: RAG-CSI: Global Local Retrieval via Joint State and Dynamics Matching for CSI Prediction
papers.summary: Channel state information (CSI) prediction forecasts future channel states from historical observations, supporting transceiver design and resource allocation with reduced measurement overhead. However, existing deep learning predictors mainly encode channel knowledge in model parameters, which can limit their ability to represent diverse patterns of channel dynamics across scenes. In this paper, we propose RAG-CSI, a retrieval-enhanced Transformer framework that augments prediction with relevant historical channel knowledge. Specifically, we construct a global--local CSI knowledge store containing representative observations across scenes and historical observations from the current serving scene. We further develop joint state--dynamics retrieval (JSDR), which jointly characterizes channel states, phase dynamics, and amplitude dynamics to retrieve relevant CSI sequences. A Transformer predictor then uses cross-attention to fuse the retrieved knowledge with the current CSI history and predict future CSI with limited additional model parameters. Experiments on a multi-scene CSI dataset show overall improvements exceeding 10\% across all five evaluation metrics over the best baseline for each metric, including a 15.42\% reduction in normalized mean squared error.

papers.title: JEPA-Inspired Latent Field Prediction for Sparse-Pilot MIMO-OFDM Channel Reconstruction
papers.summary: Accurate acquisition of full channel state information (CSI) is essential for multiple-input multiple-output orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (MIMO-OFDM) wireless systems, while dense pilot-based estimation incurs substantial overhead. Directly minimizing the prediction error over raw CSI coefficients is fragile in realistic propagation environments, since small-scale fading, mobility, local scattering, and small spatial perturbations can induce large phase-sensitive variations. Nevertheless, wireless channels contain strong spatial, temporal, and frequency-domain correlations that can be more predictably represented in a latent propagation-field domain. Motivated by this observation, we propose a joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA)-inspired field world model, defined as a latent predictive model of the wireless propagation field, for sparse-pilot channel reconstruction. The model maps CSI observations into latent time-frequency tokens, predicts masked or future latent field states from historical multi-band context, and fuses the predicted latent prior with sparse noisy current pilots to reconstruct the full MIMO-OFDM channel. Ray-tracing experiments show that the proposed method improves normalized mean square error (NMSE) over pilot-only and direct reconstruction baselines, supporting latent field prediction as an effective prior for sparse-pilot channel acquisition.

papers.title: SuperJEPA: Pretraining with a Supervision-Augmented Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture for High Energy Physics
papers.summary: Foundation models often obtain powerful results through very large unlabeled training datasets that dwarf available labeled datasets in size, but high energy physics already provides large samples of high-fidelity labeled simulation. We therefore ask whether self-supervised objectives improve over supervised pretraining alone when large labeled samples already exist. We introduce SuperJEPA, a joint-embedding predictive architec- ture augmented with a supervised objective, and find improved downstream jet-tagging performance across multiple tasks, model sizes, and pretraining dataset sizes. The gains persist for both frozen and fine-tuned encoders, motivating predictive self-supervision in future large-scale particle-physics foundation models.

papers.title: The proton structure one mode at a time: a Neural Tangent Kernel analysis of a DIS fit
papers.summary: We study the training dynamics of a feed-forward neural network (NN) through the analysis of the neural tangent kernel (NTK) in a phenomenologically relevant fit of parton distribution functions (PDFs) from deep inelastic scattering (DIS) data. The exact integration of the gradient flow derived in a previous single-flavour analysis is generalised to the multi-flavour case, yielding an analytical perspective on the relationship between data and methodology during training. The Shapley value recently used in the context of PDFs is derived within our statistical framework for observables that depend linearly on the PDFs, and we outline a geometric interpretation of training. We expose the role of gradient-based optimisation algorithms and of the parametrisation in the regularisation of the ill-posed inverse problem that affects the determination of PDFs from experimental data, demonstrating that the regularisation amounts to the incremental inclusion of NTK modes, each learned at the timescale set by the corresponding eigenvalue. We find that only a few leading modes of the NTK are necessary to reconstruct the target PDFs, while the noise of the data is carried by the sub-leading ones learned at later stages of training. Finally, we consider the impact of the initialisation on the training dynamics, and recover a transient behaviour observed in the previous analysis and in the machine learning (ML) literature. Beyond sharpening our understanding of the training dynamics, our framework can be applied to other parametrisations (such as fixed functional forms) and ML applications in physics, as well as to stress tests in the presence of inconsistent data.

papers.title: What the Primary Lund Plane Omits: A Model-Stitching Diagnosis of a Jet-Tagger Representation Gap
papers.summary: Lund-plane and Particle Transformer (ParT) jet taggers can differ in performance because one representation is weaker, or because a weaker downstream computation reads an adequate one. Standalone performance cannot separate these. Model stitching can: it links the frozen early layers of one network to the frozen late layers of another through a single trained linear map. As a positive control we use an incomplete Lund representation, the primary declustering branch, whose deficit is known independently. Stitched into ParT's downstream, it reaches a background rejection at least as much as its own downstream recovers, yet far below ParT's background rejection: the deficit is representational, not computational. A hypergraph reader over splitting triplets does no better, ruling out higher-order correlations as the cause. The gap is invisible in AUC, which stays within 1\% of its target value, and appears only in background rejection at low signal efficiency. It localizes to 0.6\% of background jets, at and above the top mass, with more constituents but fewer primary splittings than typical background. Rebuilding the representation on the full Cambridge/Aachen declustering tree repairs the deficit as predicted: standalone rejection rises, closing 72\% of the gap. Masking nodes at inference shows the repaired network still relies almost entirely on the primary branch; the secondary splittings make the representation learnable rather than supplying information it reads. Along the primary branch, the widest-angle splitting, near the top and $W$ opening angles, is worth nearly twice a random one. For quark/gluon tagging the primary branch is far less deficient, retaining 77.6\% of ParT's rejection (46.9\% for top), and the full tree closes only 33\% of the gap (72\% for top).

papers.title: The Geometry of Manifold Learning: Singular foliations via Deep Learning models
papers.summary: Deep learning algorithms have become widely used and successful across a wide range of tasks. A key challenge is determining whether these algorithms truly capture the intrinsic geometry of their training data in order to better understand what they learn from data. In this theoretical work, we explore a new geometric structure defined on the data space by a trained neural network through the Data Information Matrix (DIM), a variation of the Fisher Information Matrix. This new geometric structure is a foliation and the main focus of this work is to explore the non-smooth case of ReLU activation functions, where traditional geometric tools often fail. The foliation is defined through a distribution spanned by the columns of the DIM. We first prove that this distribution is non-smooth in the sense of distributions, rendering the existence of an associated foliation much more complex. To circumvent this issue, we introduce a smoothed version of this distribution that differs from the original only on a set of measure zero. Finally, we prove that this smoothed distribution induces a singular foliation on the data space, which is based on the data the network has been trained with. Our theoretical contributions provide a geometric framework to better understand how neural networks organize their input space in non-smooth settings, bridging differential geometry and deep learning theory.

papers.title: Building Mathematical Software -- Lessons from the Development of GAP
papers.summary: Mathematical software has particular needs that are not all covered by the existing literature on software engineering or algorithm design. This paper looks at some of these aspects, in the concrete context of the computer algebra system GAP. It also studies the potential impact AI systems could have on the development process for mathematical software.

papers.title: Balanced Active Subspaces for Optimal Control via Trajectory Optimization
papers.summary: The curse of dimensionality associated with solving the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation for the value function remains a key obstacle for real-time optimal feedback control of high-dimensional nonlinear dynamical systems. This is especially severe in aerospace applications such as relaminarizing unsteady turbulent flows and recovering from aerodynamic stall where nonlinear dynamics play a significant role. We introduce Balanced Active Subspaces for Optimal Control (BASOC), a model reduction framework which seeks to find directions in state space along which the value function is most sensitive, and the distribution of states exhibits maximum variance along optimal trajectories. BASOC leverages trajectory optimization and the Pontryagin minimum principle to obtain state and co-state (value function gradient) data along locally optimal trajectories for constructing state and gradient covariance matrices. Balancing these matrices provides an oblique projection for approximating the value function, which can also be used to construct reduced-order models and surrogate feedback control laws. We show that for linear-quadratic optimal control problems, BASOC becomes equivalent to a snapshot method for initial condition balancing of the optimally controlled closed-loop realization. The framework is demonstrated on a nonlinear three-dimensional system where POD and balanced truncation are known to perform poorly, and on the nonlinear complex Ginzburg-Landau equation to demonstrate feasibility for larger-scale systems.

papers.title: Frequency-Uniform Log-Regret Reinforcement Learning for Diffusions
papers.summary: High-frequency control problems are often studied through time discretization, but refining the timestep $δ$ increases the discrete horizon $H=T/δ$ and can make standard finite-horizon regret guarantees deteriorate even when the physical horizon $T$ is fixed. We study episodic value-based reinforcement learning for Euler discretizations of controlled diffusions. The performance is measured as the cumulative regret over $K$ episodes relative to the optimal policy of the corresponding Euler model. Under stability and regularity conditions on value function gradients, Bellman residual derivatives, and fitted critics, we prove an $\mathcal{O}(\log K)$ regret bound with constants uniform in $δ$. For dynamics with drift linear in unknown parameters and unknown constant diffusion covariance, we verify localized versions of these conditions for a constrained, model-based controlled-diffusion fitted-$Q$ algorithm (CD-FQ) and obtain high-probability $\mathcal{O}(\log K\log\log K)$ regret for fixed and finite $T$, again with constants uniform in $δ$.
papers.title_zh: 用于扩散过程的频率一致对数遗憾强化学习
papers.abstract_zh: 高频控制问题通常通过时间离散化来研究，但细化时间步长 $δ$ 会增加离散时域 $H=T/δ$，并且即使物理时域 $T$ 固定，也可能使标准的有限时域遗憾保证变差。我们研究针对受控扩散过程的 Euler 离散化的分幕式基于价值的强化学习。性能以相对于相应 Euler 模型的最优策略、在 $K$ 个分幕上的累积遗憾来衡量。在关于值函数梯度、Bellman 残差导数和拟合评判器的稳定性和正则性条件下，我们证明了一个 $\mathcal{O}(\log K)$ 遗憾界，其常数关于 $δ$ 一致。对于漂移关于未知参数线性且扩散协方差为未知常数的动力学，我们针对一种受约束的、基于模型的受控扩散拟合-$Q$ 算法（CD-FQ）验证了这些条件的局部化版本，并在固定且有限的 $T$ 下获得了高概率 $\mathcal{O}(\log K\log\log K)$ 遗憾，同样其常数关于 $δ$ 一致。

papers.title: Regression Functions as Fields on Covariate Space: Evolution Equations, the Hessian, and Identification
papers.summary: For each time $t$, the regression function $m_t(x)=E[Y_t\mid X_t=x]$ of an outcome on contemporaneous covariates can be regarded as a field on covariate space. We study how this field evolves when the covariates of individual units move as a diffusion and the outcome attached to each unit changes according to its own dynamics. Under mild regularity we show that $m_t$ satisfies a second-order evolution equation whose diffusion term is $\frac12\mathrm{tr}(Σ\nabla^2 m_t)$, the trace of the Hessian of the regression function weighted by the instantaneous covariance $Σ$ of the covariate increments, whose transport term is the drift of the time-reversed covariate process, and whose source term is the conditional mean rate of change of the outcome. The equation is a regression-theoretic reading of a classical transport law, and it yields a Feynman-Kac representation of $m_t$ along reversed covariate paths. We connect the Hessian appearing in the equation to the Hessian estimated by quadratic regression (under Gaussian design the best quadratic approximation has Hessian $E[\nabla^2 m(X)]$ exactly) and to the leading bias of kernel smoothers. For binary outcomes governed by bistable replicator dynamics with imitation among units with similar covariates, the closed equation is of Nagumo type, its planar travelling fronts are exactly logistic in $(x,t)$, and a single logistic regression of the outcome on covariates and time identifies the ratio of diffusion to reaction and the direction of invasion. We discuss identification under panel versus repeated cross-sectional designs and a two-stage estimation strategy, and we illustrate the results with simulations.
papers.title_zh: 回归函数作为协变量空间上的场：演化方程、Hessian 与识别
papers.abstract_zh: 对于每个时刻 $t$，结果对同期协变量的回归函数 $m_t(x)=E[Y_t\mid X_t=x]$ 可以视为协变量空间上的一个场。我们研究当个体单元的协变量按扩散过程移动，且附着于每个单元的结果按其自身动态变化时，该场如何演化。在温和的正则性条件下，我们证明 $m_t$ 满足一个二阶演化方程，其扩散项为 $\frac12\mathrm{tr}(Σ\nabla^2 m_t)$，即由协变量增量的瞬时协方差 $Σ$ 加权的回归函数 Hessian 的迹，其输运项为时间反演协变量过程的漂移，其源项为结果的条件平均变化率。该方程是对一个经典输运定律的回归论解读，并给出 $m_t$ 沿反向协变量路径的 Feynman-Kac 表示。我们将方程中出现的 Hessian 与由二次回归估计的 Hessian（在高斯设计下，最佳二次逼近的 Hessian 恰为 $E[\nabla^2 m(X)]$）以及核平滑器的首阶偏差联系起来。对于由双稳态复制子动力学支配的二元结果，其中具有相似协变量的单元之间存在模仿，该封闭方程属于 Nagumo 型，其平面行波在 $(x,t)$ 中恰为 logistic 形式，而结果对协变量和时间的单次 logistic 回归可识别扩散与反应之比以及入侵方向。我们讨论面板设计与重复横截面设计下的识别以及一个两阶段估计策略，并用模拟说明结果。

papers.title: FASST: A Compact Stateless Atmosphere Model for Long-Term Ocean Coupling
papers.summary: Coupled climate simulations are computationally expensive, largely because of the atmosphere. We introduce FASST, a coupled climate model that retains the prognostic POP2 ocean while replacing the atmosphere and sea ice with lightweight U-Net emulators. The atmospheric emulator is diagnostic, predicting surface fluxes from the evolving ocean-ice state every $6$ simulated hours, while the sea-ice emulator advances the ice state monthly. For $140$ years of unforced integration, FASST maintains a stable global-mean climate without SST restoring, with post-transient global-mean SST of $291.30 \pm 0.22\mathrm{K}$ compared with $291.25 \pm 0.10\mathrm{K}$ in CESM$2$ piControl. FASST also captures interannual Niño-$3.4$ variability, although with weaker amplitude than CESM ($0.62\mathrm{K}$ versus $1.02\mathrm{K}$). These results demonstrate that a stateless learned atmosphere can sustain stable, free-running coupled climate simulations over century-scale integrations.

papers.title: Scale-aware and spatially-localised optimisation of kilometre-scale MLWP models
papers.summary: Preserving fine-scale structure without degrading spatial accuracy is a central challenge for kilometre-scale machine-learning weather prediction (MLWP). We introduce a loss based on the dual-tree complex wavelet transform that constrains atmospheric fields jointly by scale, location, and orientation. We evaluate its performance using an experimental joint global--regional FastNet configuration, which produces \SI{1.5}{km} forecasts over the UK alongside $\sim$\SI{31}{km} global forecasts. Relative to both mean-squared error (MSE) and an FFT-based spectral objective, the wavelet loss substantially improves spectral fidelity. Compared with MSE training, it maintains similar pointwise performance, improves neighbourhood-based verification, and produces sharper precipitation fields with more realistic intensity distributions. These results demonstrate that spatially localised wavelet constraints can preserve multiscale atmospheric structure while largely avoiding the loss of pointwise accuracy associated with globally supported spectral objectives.

papers.title: Expert lithological labels do not improve learning when used to predict marine sediment properties
papers.summary: Scientific drilling has produced large archives of physical, chemical and magnetic measurements linked to descriptions of the rock recovered. These archives are mostly incomplete: instruments sample at different intervals, recovery is partial, and destructive analyses preclude later measurement of the same material. We train an self-supervised embedding model on the LILY ocean drilling database using six routinely logged properties (bulk density, magnetic susceptibility, natural gamma radiation, and red, green and blue reflectance) across 236,963 observations from 296 boreholes, with a masked variational autoencoder that has a heteroscedastic Gaussian decoder and learnable mask tokens. The embeddings separate geologist-assigned lithologies as well as a variant trained with those labels, and increasing the weight on the labels degrades reconstruction while leaving classification unchanged. The labels are recoverable from the measurements geologists use to assign them, so training on them adds nothing. Lithological categories compress continuous measurements into classes, and compressing them discards what the measurements record about the processes that produced the rock. The embeddings also predict physical properties that were absent from training, on boreholes the model has never seen. While depth should account for this since sediments compact with burial, it does not. On held-out boreholes depth alone reaches a median $R^2$ of -0.02, against 0.20 for the embedding.

papers.title: Retrospective macromolecular pool fraction mapping from conventional clinical MRI: a physics-guided self-supervised deep learning framework
papers.summary: Macromolecular pool fraction (MPF) is a quantitative imaging biomarker sensitive to myelin integrity and other changes in tissue macromolecular content, but specialized acquisitions and reconstruction methods limit its use in large-scale studies. We present a physics-guided, self-supervised deep learning framework for retrospectively estimating MPF directly from conventional clinical brain MRI ($T_1$-weighted, $T_2$-weighted, and fluid-attenuated inversion recovery [FLAIR]) without paired quantitative reference scans. The framework embeds an analytical two-pool magnetization transfer signal model that related sequence-averaged radiofrequency transmit power to apparent longitudinal relaxation. To accommodate heterogeneous clinical protocols, the network conditions intermediate features on acquisition parameters via adaptive instance normalization. It was trained and evaluated on a multisite, multivendor, multiprotocol dataset of 7,705 MRI sessions (3 T). Across 1,237 test sessions, mean MPF was $0.182 \pm 0.007$ in white matter and $0.144 \pm 0.009$ in gray matter, with limited variation across vendor-by-protocol groups (between-group coefficient of variation: 2.65% and 5.63%, respectively). In 70 sessions with demyelinating-disease labels, MPF was 35.6% lower in segmented lesions than in normal-appearing white matter. MPF maps from two different clinical protocols acquired in a healthy volunteer showed a mean voxel-wise absolute percentage difference of 7.7% and a concordance correlation coefficient of $0.888$, indicating good cross-protocol consistency. These results suggest that magnetization transfer-informed self-supervised learning enables stable MPF mapping from conventional clinical MRI, providing a scalable approach to investigate demyelinating pathology in both existing imaging archives and prospectively acquired conventional clinical scans without dedicated qMT acquisitions.

papers.title: Feedback autocratic strategies in stochastic games
papers.summary: A stochastic game is an optimal control problem for multiple agents in a stochastic environment. Stochastic games contain important practical problems, related to environmental issues or traffic flows. If the number of environmental states is one, such stochastic games are called repeated games. In repeated games, several strategies which unilaterally control payoffs have been proposed, and these strategies work in a mechanism similar to feedback control. In this paper, we generalize these strategies as feedback strategies in stochastic games, and investigate their properties. In particular, we provide a necessary and sufficient condition for such feedback strategies to work as controllers of payoffs under some assumptions. We demonstrate the performance of such feedback strategies in several examples related to social dilemmas. Our findings connect the theory of payoff control in repeated games to the theory of feedback control in stochastic games.

papers.title: Enhancing Clinical Classifier Robustness with Deep Representation Learning Based OOD Detection on DNA Methylation Data
papers.summary: DNA methylation (DNAM) array-based tumor classification is a powerful clinical diagnostic tool, but models trained on fixed reference cohorts can produce faulty predictions for tumor types not represented in the training distribution. We propose an end-to-end deep representation learning-based out-of-distribution (OOD) detection framework for DNAm array data. Deep neural network (DNN) classifiers were trained on public sarcoma (SARC) (GSE140686) and brain tumor (BT) (GSE90496) cohorts, and feature vectors were extracted from bottleneck layers. Five OOD methods, including 1dimension (1D)-Subspace Analysis (1D-SSA), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Ridge Regression, Mahalanobis Distance (MD), and Sum of Squared Distances (SSD), were explored with 200 and 500-dimensional embeddings. Spectral discrepancy was used to discriminate in-distribution (IND) from OOD samples. Performance was measured via cross-validation, holdout samples, and an independent clinical dataset. 1D-SSA was the most effective approach. In the sarcoma-IND/brain tumor-OOD setting, the framework achieved an AUROC of 0.975 and True Negative Rate (TNR)@95TPR of 0.930, and an AUROC of 0.9569 and TNR@95TPR of 0.8660 for the brain tumor-IND/sarcoma-OOD setting. On the independent clinical test set, the method yielded a mean AUROC of 0.976, a DE of 0.032, an FPR@95TPR of 0.065, and a TNR@95TPR of 0.935. These results show deep representation-based OOD detection as a practical quality-control layer for clinical-grade methylation-based tumor classification systems.

papers.title: HELICS: Biobank-scale Conditional Synthetic Genome Generation via Latent Flow Matching
papers.summary: Individual-level genotype data underpin genetic discovery, disease-risk modeling, and therapeutic development, yet many critical settings remain data-limited, including underrepresented ancestries, rare or imbalanced disease cohorts, and restricted-access biobanks. Conditional synthetic genome generation would support privacy-aware benchmarking, simulation, and data augmentation, but requires learning an ultra-high-dimensional discrete distribution over hundreds of thousands to tens of millions of correlated single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs), or sites of DNA variation. We introduce HELICS: High-fidelity gEneration via Latent Interpolant Conditional Synthesis, a phasing-free latent flow matching framework for genome-wide SNP-level generation from biobank-scale genotype data. HELICS tokenizes chromosomes with convolutional autoencoders, reducing >600K SNPs to 4,096 continuous latent tokens, and trains a transformer parameterized conditional flow matching model over the concatenated multi-chromosome latent representation. Trained on over 417K genomes in the UK Biobank, HELICS generates genome-wide common-variant synthetic cohorts without haplotype phasing and achieves stronger fidelity to real genotypes than existing haplotype-based simulators, including high allele-frequency agreement in external evaluation and superior preservation of local and long-range SNP correlation structure. Conditioning on ancestry and genetic liability summaries enables targeted generation across genetic risk profiles; in perturbation analyses, by increasing the conditioned disease trait liability, HELICS induces SNP-level dosage changes in generated genomes that are highly correlated with published association weights. HELICS provides a scalable generative modeling framework for SNP-level genome data and a path toward conditional synthetic cohorts for data-limited genetic studies.

papers.title: Neuronal Identity as an Organizational Basis for Analyzing Neural Population Dynamics
papers.summary: Individual neurons exhibit diverse molecular, morphological, and electrophysiological properties that shape their distinct roles in neural circuits. While these multimodal features are largely shared across individuals, they remain an underutilized source of information in analyzing neural population dynamics. We posit that these shared biological profiles provide a common reference for relating neural dynamics across subjects and recording sessions. Our framework leverages this structure by routing neurons into latent groups based on their biological profiles and analyzing population dynamics through group-level representations. Because these assignments are anchored in biological properties that are consistent across subjects, the learned organization supports transfer to unseen animals without retraining or neuron-wise correspondence. We evaluate our framework on whole-brain calcium imaging in larval zebrafish and large-scale electrophysiology in the mouse visual cortex. Across both species and recording modalities, the framework delivers state-of-the-art performance in both neural decoding and manifold analysis: it achieves superior decoding of behavior and stimulus labels while better preserving the temporal consistency and local geometric structure of latent trajectories on unseen data. Our experiments demonstrate that not only does providing biological features improve baseline performance, but our proposed framework achieves even stronger results by using these properties to explicitly structure the population rather than treating them as auxiliary inputs. Together, these results suggest that organizing neural populations by their multimodal biological features offers a promising framework for generalizing population dynamics across subjects and recording sessions.

papers.title: Every route counts, but some count more: a max-plus view of the C. elegans brain
papers.summary: Brains do not simply add up every signal they receive: they select which routes dominate. Yet connectomes are usually analyzed with tools that sum over all paths and place neural states in Euclidean spaces, blurring the feedback circuits that may sustain internal states. Here we treat neural signaling as routing instead of diffusion and describe it with max-plus algebra, in which signals accumulate along a path and the strongest route prevails. We propose a model in which the functional connectome of Caenorhabditis elegans emerges from the time-varying combination of electrical, synaptic, monoaminergic, neuropeptidergic and hormonal layers, and analyze five networks within this framework. Each collapses onto a handful of dominant feedback loops, which recover well-characterized circuits and point to new candidates for experimental study. Unlike linear spectra, these structures keep the biological meaning of the data, and their order-based description suggests that brain states live in lattices rather than Euclidean spaces.
papers.title_zh: 每条路径都重要，但有些路径更重要：秀丽隐杆线虫大脑的极大加视角
papers.abstract_zh: 大脑并非简单地将接收到的每个信号相加：它们会选择哪些路径占主导。然而，连接组通常使用对所有路径求和、并将神经状态置于欧几里得空间的工具进行分析，从而模糊了可能维持内部状态的反馈环路。在这里，我们将神经信号传递视为路由而非扩散，并用极大加代数来描述它；在极大加代数中，信号沿路径累积，最强的路径胜出。我们提出一个模型，其中秀丽隐杆线虫的功能连接组由电、突触、单胺能、神经肽能和激素层的时间变化组合而涌现，并在该框架内分析五个网络。每个网络都坍缩为少数几个占主导的反馈环路，这些环路重现了已充分表征的神经回路，并指向可供实验研究的新候选对象。与线性谱不同，这些结构保留了数据的生物学意义，并且其基于序的描述表明，大脑状态存在于格中，而非欧几里得空间中。

papers.title: Structure, Not Sequence: Tracking and Validating Folding Mechanisms in ESMFold's Trunk with Sparse Autoencoders
papers.summary: Structure predictors like ESMFold fold proteins using neural network computation and have transformed structural biology. However, the driving mechanism from amino-acid (AA) sequence to 3D structure is insufficiently understood, and biological meaning remains locked in the dense network. Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) have shown promising results in obtaining interpretable concept features over an overcomplete basis of intermediate protein sequence-model representations. Yet folding models, which predict physical shape from AA sequence semantics, have no such account. We hypothesize that the features carrying the folding computation evolve in the 3D structural regression process. In this paper, we interpret the folding trunk in three steps. First, a pilot analysis on the representation distribution across modules and recycles locates distinct spatial computation in the trunk. Second, the dictionaries expose a division of labor: the single representation carries inherited semantics, and the pair representation computes the pairwise geometry. Third, we interpret the dictionary at scale with a reasoning language model, trace how the concepts compose across blocks by gradient-based attribution, and follow the interpreted code to the model's folding output, verifying where the computation aligns with, or departs from, known biochemistry. Together, the sparse dictionaries we train capture the relational geometry the trunk computes beyond the sequence model, and their concept activations forecast the model's own fold quality, turning the black-box folding trunk into a sparse, interpretable, and scientifically verifiable circuit.

papers.title: HGPRGDel: GPR-Aware Learning and Ranking for Growth-Coupled Gene Deletion Design
papers.summary: Designing microbial strains for growth-coupled production, in which cellular growth is linked to the synthesis of a target compound through genetic interventions, is a fundamental goal in metabolic engineering. Constraint-based methods can identify growth-coupled deletion strategies, but design for each target typically requires a separate search across a large number of possible gene-deletion combinations. This motivates a reusable approach that learns from previously evaluated strain designs to prioritize candidate interventions before downstream constraint-based evaluation. We present a reproducible protocol for growth-coupled gene deletion design that learns and ranks gene-deletion priorities for each target metabolite. Using computationally curated deletion strategies as learning resources, the protocol generates continuous deletion-priority rankings, constructs candidate strategies at adjustable search-space budgets, and evaluates these candidates through constraint-based metabolic analysis. Its learning component, HGPRGDel, explicitly represents gene-protein-reaction (GPR) logic, capturing how multiple genes can jointly support a reaction or alternative genes can maintain its activity, while integrating molecular and reaction-level information. Across e_coli_core, iMM904, and iML1515, the protocol achieves the highest macro-F1 and AUC among the evaluated learning configurations. HGPRGDel's rankings recovered an average of 90% of the reference deletion genes from MetNetComp by examining fewer genes than the evaluated baseline methods. By separating learned intervention prioritization from downstream constraint-based assessment, the protocol provides a reproducible framework for reusing strain-design knowledge while controlling the size of the candidate space and retaining mechanistic evaluation of growth-coupled production.

papers.title: Quantum Evolution Kernel for Node-Attributed Graphs
papers.summary: We present a novel approach to embed node-attributed graphs onto neutral-atom quantum computers, and propose an application to digit recognition. Our approach extends PASQAL's quantum evolution kernel (QEK) by introducing a node-level feature encoding based on three-level quantum states.
